context_build.causal_mechanism: Test whether the market is treating an RBA-over-RBNZ regime as a one-way AUDNZD trend when the actual mechanism is two-sided. Australia is already transmitting tighter policy through housing (stamp-duty receipts and home values down) while AONIA still prices additional hikes. New Zealand printed a Q2 GDP beat and passed an India FTA, yet NZDUSD remains near a 5-year low. If the housing channel caps the RBA or NZ data stops being ignored, AUDNZD's extreme is a fat left tail. If energy and global tightening keep AONIA bid, the same extreme can squeeze higher. Options, not spot, own that distribution.

Spot shorts have squeeze risk; spot longs fade a policy-supported trend with no timing. The wrong priced assumption is that event risk in this cross is small because realized vol has been small.

trade.thesis: FACT: AUDNZD is at a 5-year extreme because NZDUSD collapsed, not because AUDUSD broke out; AU housing is showing the tightening channel while AONIA still prices about +21.5bp by October and about +59.5bp by August 2027; NZ GDP beat and an India FTA have not reversed NZD; NZ yields are missing; Fed and BoJ hikes are delivered; USDJPY 20-day RV is 11.04 versus AUDNZD 5.09; VIX crushed to 15.44 on 17 Sep; no FX option marks exist. INFERENCE: the market is pricing a one-way RBA-over-RBNZ regime that is internally inconsistent, so the next move is a distribution with a delayed mean-reversion tail and a squeeze tail. Spot is dominated because timing is uncertain and event risk (housing prints, residual RBA path, NZ data, energy, global hike follow-through) is two-sided after realized FX vol on this cross stayed near 5%. Buying USDJPY vol after a +1.41% BoJ day is not the same trade: that realized has already printed. UNKNOWN: 3M ATMF IV, 25-delta risk-reversal, quoted premium, and the RBNZ curve — all must be checked before any OPEN. The paper book therefore HOLDs; the debate trade is still the put.
trade.mispricing: Compressed ~5% realized vol at a 5-year AUDNZD extreme is being treated as evidence that event risk is small. The packet cannot quote implied vol, so this is not an IV-versus-RV call. It is a claim that linear spot understates two-way policy/housing risk and that a long put is the expression that owns the left tail without uncapped squeeze risk.
